subject: Holosync load & latency acceptance — implementation handoff
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Cho <emily.cho@holosync.ai>, Rajiv Suri <rajiv.suri@holosync.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Holosync load & latency acceptance — implementation handoff

Hi Emily / Rajiv,

Great to meet you both on Friday — thanks again for the productive demo. Per our call, we're ready to move from onboarding discovery into an acceptance-run that will validate latency/throughput at your peak request patterns before we flip the production routing.

Attached is a concise benchmark plan that outlines:
- SLO targets we agreed on (p95 latency, 99th tail, and sustained RPS ranges)
- Load-shape scenarios (baseline, spiky day, batch reprocessing)
- Test harness artifacts & run scripts we will provide
- Roles and outcomes for the acceptance gate (pass/fail criteria)

Key asks for Holosync:
1) Confirm which LLM variant you'll exercise (open model name + model size) so we can align quantization/runtime configs.
2) Provide a small representative prompt corpus (200-500 requests) by Wed so we can seed the KV cache and warm the system with realistic distributions.
3) Approve the two-day window for the acceptance run: Aug 7–8 (we'll reserve Dedicated capacity).

Monica / Michael — looping you in to coordinate Dedicated pool sizing, run orchestration, and post-run artifact collection. My goal is to produce a single acceptance artifact (timestamped logs, latency histograms, token counts, and a short verdict doc) that Holosync can archive for procurement.

Attachments: holosync-benchmark-plan.pdf (full plan), holosync-run-scripts.tar.gz (runner + load profiles)

Thanks —
Jordan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com]
From: Emily Cho <emily.cho@holosync.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rajiv Suri <rajiv.suri@holosync.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 Jul 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Holosync load & latency acceptance — implementation handoff

Jordan,

Thanks — plan looks thorough. A few clarifications before we lock the window: 

- Model: we'll use gpt-neox-20b-quant (open variant) for the primary run and gpt-neox-6b as the fallback for lower-cost comparison.
- Prompt corpus: Rajiv will drop a zipped corpus (csv) by EOD Thursday.
- Capacity: the Aug 7–8 window works but if you need a dry-run we'd appreciate a short smoke on Aug 3 (non-business hours).

Acceptance targets we want to see in the report: 
- P95 generation latency <= 350ms for single-turn prompts (avg token length ~18)
- 99th percentile tail <= 900ms under sustained 250 RPS for 30m buckets
- Throughput: sustained 3k tokens/sec overall without error spikes

If you can confirm Dedicated pool sizing and the smoke-run timing, we'll sign off on the window and upload the corpus. Also please flag any special headers/trace IDs we should include so our observability team can align logs.

Best,
Emily
Head of Platform | Holosync AI
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Jul 2028 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Holosync load & latency acceptance — implementation handoff

Folks — forwarding Emily's reply + Holosync targets. Quick plan:

Action items (internal):
- Monica: Please provision Dedicated pool with the following spec: 6x A100-80GB equivalent nodes (we'll oversubscribe if possible) and enable KV-prefix caching for the warm phase.
- Michael: Schedule a 2hr smoke-run on Aug 3 at 01:00–03:00 PDT (off-hours). Keep it low-risk: 50 RPS bursts + end-to-end traces.
- Marissa: Own runbook & evidence collection — capture token-level cost, p95/p99 histograms, and an artifact bundle (logs + perf graphs). Use the acceptance-checklist template.

Notes on test behavior:
- We'll run three scenarios: warmup (15m), sustained-run (30m windows at 250 RPS), then a spike window (2x-3x for 5m bursts).
- Use the provided gpt-neox-20b-quant profile; fall back to 6b for the cost-comparison pass.

Monica — can you confirm pool sizing and whether autoscaling credit is needed? Also call out any constraints if the Dedicated cluster overlaps another customer's scheduled runs.

I'll draft an internal run schedule and share the Drive folder link with Holosync once we confirm.

-Jordan

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Emily Cho <emily.cho@holosync.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jul 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Holosync load & latency acceptance — implementation handoff

Jordan / team / Emily —

Thanks for the clear ask. Confirming capacity and the orchestration plan:

1) Dedicated pool sizing: provisioned 6x A100-80GB equivalent nodes with a reserved throughput profile. We'll mark the pool "Holosync-Acceptance" for Aug 3 (smoke) and Aug 7–8 (full). Autoscaling will be disabled during the acceptance windows to keep results deterministic; burst nodes will be manually added if we observe sustained saturation.

2) Trace headers: use X-Redwood-Trace-ID and X-Holosync-Run for all runner traffic — Emily, if you can echo X-Holosync-Run in your corpus we'll map logs server-side.

3) Artifacts & evidence checklist (attached acceptance-checklist.xlsx):
- Timestamped perf CSVs (1s resolution)
- P95/P99 histograms per-minute
- Error-rate by origin and by token index
- Full kernel selection logs & quantization flags used
- Runner seed + script hash for reproducibility

4) Smoke-run on Aug 3 @ 01:00–03:00 PDT is scheduled. Michael — please run the smoke pipeline, upload the artifacts to the Drive folder, and post a short readout (15–20 slides) in the shared folder within 6 hours of completion.

Attachments included: holosync-acceptance-checklist.xlsx (checklist), holosync-benchmark-plan.pdf (versioned), holosync-run-scripts.tar.gz (scripts)

Emily — once Rajiv uploads the corpus we'll run a local warm run and share a short preflight readout so Holosync can confirm model behavior. If anything looks off we can iterate on batch sizes / prefix caching before the main run.

Monica Patel
Sr. Implementation Manager | Redwood Inference
[monica.patel@redwoodinference.com]
